title: digitalis purpurea var. longipedunculata
intro: Digitalis purpurea var. longipedunculata, commonly known as Foxglove, is a biennial plant in the family Plantaginaceae, characterized by its tall spikes of tubular bells. The plant is known for its health benefits, including the treatment of heart conditions such as atrial fibrillation and congestive heart failure, due to its ability to increase the force of heart contractions. The therapeutic actions of Foxglove are attributed to its digitalis glycosides, which act as positive inotropes and have a direct effect on the heart muscle. The bioactive constituents of Foxglove include cardiac glycosides, specifically digitoxin and digoxin, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
